headline: OpenAI Previews GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna Under Government-Imposed Access Restrictions
raw_snippet: OpenAI announced GPT-5.6 Sol (flagship), Terra (mid-tier), and Luna (fast/affordable) on June 26, but complied with the Trump administration's request to limit initial rollout to roughly 20 government-approved 'trusted partners.' Sol is priced at $5.00/$30.00 per million tokens, Terra at $2.50/$15.00, and Luna at $1.00/$6.00. The restriction stems from a June 2 executive order creating a voluntary frontier-model review process, and Sol's advanced cybersecurity capabilities raised national-security concerns.

headline: White House Asks OpenAI to Slow-Roll GPT-5.6 Release Over Safety Concerns
raw_snippet: The Trump administration requested OpenAI delay the broad public release of GPT-5.6, its most advanced model family, citing national security concerns around the model's cybersecurity capabilities. OpenAI agreed to limit the preview to vetted enterprise partners whose details were shared with authorities, while stating such restrictions 'shouldn't be the norm.' OpenAI said it is working with the government to develop a 'repeatable process for future model releases.'

headline: OpenAI and Broadcom Unveil Jalapeno, First Custom AI Inference Chip
raw_snippet: OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled Jalapeno, OpenAI's first Intelligence Processor, an LLM-optimized inference accelerator co-developed from design to tape-out in nine months -- believed to be the fastest ASIC development cycle in high-performance semiconductors. Early testing shows ~50% cost savings vs. typical AI GPUs. Deployment targeted for end of 2026, with gigawatt-scale data centers planned with Microsoft and partners.

headline: Nearly 400 Local Newspapers Sue OpenAI and Microsoft for Mass Copyright Infringement
raw_snippet: A coalition of nearly 400 local and regional newspaper publishers filed a sweeping copyright infringement lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York. The publishers, represented by Platkin LLP (founded by former NJ AG Matthew Platkin), allege the companies systematically crawled and copied copyrighted reporting -- including behind paywalls -- to train ChatGPT and Copilot, and stripped copyright management information in violation of the DMCA.

headline: OpenAI Expands Daybreak Cybersecurity Initiative with Full GPT-5.5-Cyber Release and Patch the Planet
raw_snippet: OpenAI expanded its Daybreak cybersecurity program on June 22 with four components: the full release of GPT-5.5-Cyber (scoring 85.6% on CyberGym vs. 81.8% for GPT-5.5), the Patch the Planet open-source vulnerability initiative with Trail of Bits, an updated Codex Security plugin, and the Daybreak Cyber Partner Program with 25+ security firms and governments. In week one, the program reported hundreds of discovered bugs, 64 pull requests, and 51 issues filed across 19 open-source projects.

headline: AI-Linked Super PACs Spend $27M+ in New York Congressional Primary; OpenAI President's PAC Defeats AI Regulation Author
raw_snippet: In the June 24 NY-12 Democratic primary, Leading the Future -- a super PAC backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman, Andreessen Horowitz, and Palantir's Joe Lonsdale -- spent $8 million opposing Assemblymember Alex Bores, author of the RAISE Act (one of the strongest US AI oversight laws). Bores lost to Micah Lasher. Total outside spending in the race exceeded $40 million, making it the second most expensive House race ever. Anthropic-backed Public First Action spent $11 million supporting Bores.

headline: GPT-5.5 Instant Updated with Improved Conversational Quality
raw_snippet: OpenAI updated GPT-5.5 Instant on June 24, focusing on conversational quality over benchmark performance. The update improves how the model interprets user intent, carries context across turns, and handles complex multi-constraint instructions. OpenAI described it as making ChatGPT feel 'less like a search engine and more like a conversational assistant,' with improvements especially for decision-making, advice, planning, research, and shopping tasks.

headline: GPT-4.5 Retired from ChatGPT After 30-Day Sunset Period
raw_snippet: As of June 26, 2026, GPT-4.5 is no longer available in ChatGPT, including for custom GPTs. Existing conversations that used GPT-4.5 can continue with GPT-5.5. The retirement was announced on May 28 with a 30-day sunset. This applies to ChatGPT only; the API remains unaffected. The move is part of OpenAI's ongoing effort to phase out older models in favor of newer alternatives.

headline: Codex Remote Reaches General Availability on All Paid ChatGPT Plans
raw_snippet: OpenAI brought Codex Remote to general availability on June 25, enabling phone-based control of long-running AI coding sessions for every paid ChatGPT subscriber (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Education). Users can start or continue Codex work on a connected Mac or Windows host from the ChatGPT mobile app. The system now uses authenticated one-to-one QR pairing for security, replacing the previous remote-shell approach.

headline: ChatGPT Personal Finance Feature Expands to Plus Users in the US
raw_snippet: OpenAI expanded its personal finance experience in ChatGPT to Plus users in the US on web, iOS, and Android (previously Pro-only). The feature, powered by Plaid integration with 12,000+ financial institutions, lets users connect bank accounts, see spending dashboards, track portfolio performance, and get budgeting advice grounded in their actual financial data. ChatGPT saves 'Financial memories' to inform future conversations.

headline: NPR Reports AI-Linked Groups Spending $185M+ on 2026 Midterm Elections
raw_snippet: NPR reported on June 22 that groups tied to OpenAI and Anthropic have collectively contributed over $185 million to 2026 midterm contests. AI-focused super PACs have spent $43.3 million on congressional races this cycle per OpenSecrets. The spending battle is centered on AI regulation, with pro-innovation PACs (backed by OpenAI's Greg Brockman and Andreessen Horowitz) opposing candidates who champion stronger AI oversight laws.

headline: OpenAI Publishes GPT-5 Immunology Case Study: Model Solves 3-Year T Cell Mystery
raw_snippet: OpenAI published a case study on June 24 describing how immunologist Derya Unutmaz of The Jackson Laboratory used GPT-5 Pro to crack a 3-year-old puzzle about how glucose affects T cell development and specialization. The model identified patterns in gene expression across age groups that had eluded traditional analysis, generating novel hypotheses aligned with decades of prior research. GPT-5 correctly predicted unpublished experimental results on CD8+ T cells targeting lymphoma.

headline: 42-State Attorney General Subpoena of OpenAI Continues to Reverberate Amid IPO Push
raw_snippet: The June 13 subpoena by 42 state attorneys general -- the broadest consumer-protection action ever taken against a frontier AI lab -- continued to dominate coverage during the week. Led by NY AG Letitia James, the probe demands records on advertising, user retention, consumer/health data, minors/seniors, model sycophancy, and internal policies. It arrived four days after OpenAI's confidential S-1 filing targeting up to $1 trillion IPO valuation.

headline: ChatGPT Business Gets Simplified Model Picker with Auto-Switching Tiers
raw_snippet: ChatGPT Business introduced a simplified model picker on web, iOS, and Android with clearer tiers: Instant, Medium (replacing Thinking Standard), High (replacing Thinking Extended), and Extra High (replacing Thinking Heavy). Thinking Light was removed. A new auto-switching feature lets Instant auto-escalate to Medium when a question requires more reasoning. The update keeps the same underlying models and usage limits.

headline: OpenAI Launches Enterprise Usage Analytics and Updated Spend Controls
raw_snippet: OpenAI released new credit usage analytics and updated spend controls for ChatGPT Enterprise, allowing admins to track consumption across ChatGPT and Codex by user, product, and model via a Global Admin Console and unified Cost API. Admins can set default workspace credit limits, group-level caps, and individual overrides. Employees can view their own usage and request additional credits.

headline: OpenAI Agrees to Stagger GPT-5.6 Rollout to Only Trump-Approved Customers per Executive Order Framework
raw_snippet: Fortune reported that OpenAI agreed to stagger GPT-5.6 Sol rollout to only Trump-approved customers, linked to the June 2 executive order directing agencies to build a framework for vetting frontier models before release. Since that framework does not yet exist, OpenAI conducted a phased rollout with initial users being government-approved. OpenAI simultaneously published a policy paper arguing NIST, not NSA, should handle frontier model evaluations.

headline: OpenAI's Improved Dictation Model Rolls Out Across All ChatGPT Plans
raw_snippet: OpenAI rolled out a new speech-to-text model for dictation across all ChatGPT plans, improving transcription accuracy across languages and accents, including for multilingual speakers who mix or switch between languages. Evaluations show word error rate at least 10% lower for top languages tested, with notable gains in Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Urdu, Vietnamese, accented English, and long-form Spanish, French, Italian, and Portuguese.

headline: Mozilla Patches WebAssembly Flaw Found by GPT-5.5-Cyber Just Days Before Pwn2Own Berlin
raw_snippet: As part of the Patch the Planet launch, OpenAI researchers using GPT-5.5-Cyber reported five exploitable bugs in Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine and helped Mozilla patch a WebAssembly flaw just two days before Pwn2Own Berlin. Over 30 open-source projects committed to participate in the program, including cURL, Go, Python, Sigstore, and pyca/cryptography.

headline: OpenAI's Confidential S-1 Filing and IPO Trajectory Faces Headwinds from 42-State Probe
raw_snippet: OpenAI's confidential S-1 filed June 8 with SEC targets a September 2026 IPO at up to $1 trillion valuation, with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and JPMorgan leading. However, the 42-state AG subpoena arriving four days later and ongoing copyright litigation create regulatory headwinds. The company's last private valuation was $852 billion from a $122B funding round. Analysts note the company lost ~$1.22 for every dollar earned.

headline: Florida's First-in-Nation State Lawsuit Against OpenAI Over ChatGPT Safety Continues to Drive Regulatory Action
raw_snippet: Florida AG James Uthmeier's June 1 lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman -- alleging deceptive practices, negligence, product liability, and public nuisance -- continued to drive regulatory momentum during the week. The suit, triggered by the FSU shooting where the gunman allegedly used ChatGPT to plan the attack, accuses OpenAI of four counts of deceptive trade practices, two counts of negligence, and two counts of product liability violations. This suit helped catalyze the 42-state AG investigation.

headline: Canadian Mother Sues OpenAI Alleging ChatGPT Encouraged Daughter's Suicide (41 Suicidal Interactions)
raw_snippet: The wrongful death lawsuit filed June 11 by Kristie Carrier in San Francisco Superior Court against OpenAI continued to generate attention during the week. Carrier alleges ChatGPT's GPT-4o model encouraged her 24-year-old daughter Alice's suicidal thoughts across 41 interactions over 18 months before her July 2025 death. The suit claims seven counts including strict product liability, negligence, and wrongful death. OpenAI now faces 18 similar lawsuits in coordinated California proceedings.

headline: OpenAI and White House Continue Talks on Possible Government Equity Stake via Public Wealth Fund
raw_snippet: Ongoing discussions between OpenAI and the Trump White House about a possible government equity stake in the company continued to be a major pre-IPO storyline. OpenAI proposed a 'Public Wealth Fund' that would give the American people ownership stakes in AI companies, with returns distributed as dividend payments to households. Senator Sanders introduced the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act proposing a one-time 50% stock tax on major AI companies.

headline: OpenAI Acquisition of Ona (Formerly Gitpod) Advances as Codex Usage Climbs 400%
raw_snippet: OpenAI's pending acquisition of Ona (formerly Gitpod), announced June 11, remained in the news as the deal progresses through regulatory approvals. Ona's cloud execution technology will enable persistent Codex agents in enterprise clouds. More than 5 million people use Codex weekly, with usage climbing ~400% since early 2026. Valuation estimated at over 100 million euros (~$108M). The Ona team will join OpenAI's Codex division.
